replies:
Fit, structure and quick scripts you can use in the room — ready now for a 45–60 minute final that mixes behavioral, deal discussion and technical checks. I assume the interview is 45–60 minutes, on video, with 1–3 senior bankers and a case or deal discussion. Tell me if that’s wrong.
What they want to see, fast
- Fit: clear, specific motivation for M&A/advisory and why Lincoln (boutique exposure, sector focus, deal responsibility). Tie to 1–2 real reasons.
- Judgment & ownership: examples where you ran analyses, owned deliverables, and made tradeoffs.
- Technical competence: clean accounting walk-throughs, DCF/LBO basics, and quick sanity checks.
- Communication: short, structured answers; give a one-line takeaway, then the evidence.
- Coachability/team signals: humility, quick learning, and client focus.
Two-minute intro (use at the start or for “Tell me about yourself”)
- 0–30s: Current role and one-line top achievement: “I’m [title] at [employer], where I work on [type of deals/analyses]; I led [specific deliverable] that [result].”
- 30–75s: Two strengths illustrated with quick evidence (e.g., modelling speed + a number; diligence/workstreams managed).
- 75–110s: Why Lincoln — two specifics (deal types, boutique exposure to seniors, sector fit) and what you want next (own models, client exposure).
- Final 5–10s: One-sentence closing: “I’m excited to bring that to Lincoln because [concise reason].”
STAR answers — short templates to memorize (say each in 45–90s)
1) Owned a deliverable under tight deadline
- S: [deal context]
- T: Deliver X by Y date
- A: Prioritized, simplified model, checked key assumptions with manager
- R: Delivered on time; [quantified outcome or what decision it enabled]
Two-sentence memorization rewrite to practice.

2) Found an error others missed
- S: [analysis/deal]
- T: Ensure model accuracy
- A: Reconciled to source, traced P&L to footnotes, fixed the item
- R: Avoided a [risk], improved decision quality (one metric or consequence)
3) Conflict with a teammate
- S: Quick context
- T: Maintain timeline and quality
- A: Asked for data, proposed compromise, tested both options
- R: Kept the deal on track and improved the solution

4) Learned quickly to finish a task
- S: New sector/tool with tight timeline
- T: Produce a usable analysis
- A: Identified core concepts, built a small test model, validated with manager
- R: Delivered on time and reused the approach later
Technical checklist — be able to explain each in 30–90s
- Walk through a DCF: revenue → unlevered free cash flow → discounting → terminal value; which assumptions move value most and why.
- LBO basics: sources & uses, layering debt, covenant/interest impacts, modeling exit and IRR.
- From revenue to free cash flow: P&L → working capital movements → capex → tax adjustments.
- Why comps vs precedent transactions give different multiples; what drives a control premium.
- Simple sanity checks and quick math: percent changes, EV from EBITDA × multiple, IRR intuition.
Deal discussion — how to present a deal you worked on (3 bullets)
- One-line summary: sector, size, buyer/seller, and your role.
- Two technical points you owned (model piece, diligence item) and one challenge you solved.
- Outcome/status and one learning: what changed in your approach.

Behavioral delivery rules
- One-line answer first, then the evidence (headline → 2–3 facts → impact).
- Use numbers where possible; if you don’t have a number, say the concrete qualitative impact.
- Don’t claim things you didn’t do — precise ownership matters.
Five questions to ask them (pick three)
- How do junior analysts typically spend their time on live deals?
- What distinguishes analysts who get responsibility early here?
- Tell me about a recent deal where the team had to pivot — what changed and why?
- How do senior bankers involve analysts in client-facing moments?
- What would success look like for me in the first six months?

Common traps to avoid
- Long, unfocused answers — use structure.
- Vague claims of ownership.
- Criticizing previous employers or teammates.
- Overpromising on availability.
30-minute practice plan (do this once, aloud)
- 0–5 min: 2-minute intro out loud; refine wording.
- 5–15 min: run two STAR answers (A and B) aloud and record/relisten.
- 15–25 min: 3-minute DCF walk-through and 3-minute LBO walkthrough out loud.
- 25–30 min: rapid-fire mock: 3 behavioral prompts + 3 mental math quick checks.

If you want, next steps I can do right now
- Mock the final: I’ll ask the first question (behavioral or technical). You answer; I’ll score it on structure, evidence and specificity, give one concrete improvement, then ask the next. OR
- Draft three tailored STAR answers if you paste 1–2 short deal notes (what you did and numbers).
One assumption I made: the final round is 45–60 minutes and includes both behavioral and technical/deal discussion. Is that right?

Assuming you pick a posting, here is exactly what I will prepare on the application card for that first posting, field by field, and what I will put in each field (and what I will need from you if anything is missing). 3) Cover letter / short message (if the employer asks)
- What I will draft: a 100–250 word tailored cover letter with 2–3 bullet highlights mapping your experience to the posting's top requirements.
- What I will include as placeholders: [hiring manager name], [specific project or metric] for any employer detail you haven't given.

7) Address / City / State
- What I will put: the city and address you give, or leave as [city, state] if you don't supply one. I will use neutral entries only if the form allows (city only).
8) Work authorization / Visa status
- What I will put: the exact status you type in (U.S. citizen, Green Card, H1B, Eligible to work, etc.).
- If you don't provide it: left as [work authorization] for you to fill on the card.

9) LinkedIn URL
- What I will put: the LinkedIn URL you supply, or leave as [LinkedIn URL].

10) Portfolio / GitHub / Personal site
- What I will attach or link: any URL you supply; otherwise left blank.

11) Resume uploads / additional attachments
- What I will attach: the tailored resume PDF and the approved cover letter if requested; any other files you provide (portfolio PDF, transcripts) only after you confirm them.
12) Role-specific screening questions (yes/no, multiple choice, or short text)
- What I will draft: recommended answers based strictly on your confirmed facts or the draft facts you supplied; each answer will show as [draft answer] for you to approve or edit.
- Examples: "Are you authorized to work in the U.S.?" — I will put your explicit status; "Do you have X years experience?" — I will put the number from your confirmed facts or leave it bracketed.
13) Salary expectation / desired compensation
- What I will put: exactly what you give me (a number or range) or leave as [salary expectation]. I will not invent numbers.
- If the posting requests a range, I will show a recommended range only if you provide one.

14) Earliest start date
- What I will put: the date you provide or [earliest start date].

15) Screening essay / long-answer questions
- What I will draft: concise, tailored answers (100–300 words) mapping your experience to the question, with brackets for any missing specifics (company names, dates, metrics). You must review and approve each before submission.
16) References
- What I will put: either the references you provide (name, relationship, contact info) or leave as [references available upon request] if you prefer.

17) Equal employment opportunity / demographic questions
- What I will put: I will leave these blank or select "Prefer not to answer" unless you instruct otherwise.

18) Consent / attestation checkboxes (e.g., "I certify..."; authorize background check)
- What I will put: I will mark them only if standard (and as most applicants do); I will flag any that sound non-standard so you can confirm.
19) Resume persona / internal notes (not sent)
- What I will record: which resume persona I used, bullets highlighted, and match gaps to the posting. This helps with follow-ups and interview prep.

20) Final review summary (shown on the card before you approve)
- What I will show: every field exactly as it will be submitted to the employer, each attachment, and any bracketed items that still need your input.
What I will not do
- I will not submit the application without your explicit approval on the application card.
- I will not invent personal facts (name, email, work authorization, years) — I will show them bracketed if missing.
- I will not send anything from your email account unless you approve and the extension runs on your computer.
